messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: high rate of failed auth attempts from 35.198.22.14 across multiple token endpoints. Suspected token replay or credential stuffing. Detected in auth-proxy logs. Correlation id: c9f2-3b1e.
jen (security): I'm on it. Can someone confirm if any app logs with S3 paths were exposed around 02:12 UTC? Need to scope blast radius.
marco (oncall): seeing same in metrics. spike on /v1/authorize and /v1/session/refresh, ~1.8k reqs/min. No error percentage spike besides 401s.
kai (infra): pulling the bastion logs and auth-proxy request_snippets. small sample: ```2026-03-04T02:12:11Z auth-proxy request_id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/session/refresh status=401 src=35.198.22.14 auth_header="Bearer eyJ..."```
jen (security): copy sample. That auth_header looks like a bearer token pattern — could be leaked token replay. We need immediate mitigations: 1) block IP, 2) revoke suspected tokens, 3) rotate any service keys if found in logs, 4) notify impacted customers.
marco (oncall): blocking IP now at WAF: ```aws wafv2 update-ip-set --id ipset-zzz --addresses 35.198.22.14/32``` -- done. Confirmed WAF deny rule in place.
ops-bot: Pager assigned to @marco (oncall) for incident 1758888888 at 02:13 UTC.
marco (oncall): taking lead. @jen you own the rotation plan, @kai can you gather list of tokens active in last 24h for affected endpoints?
kai (infra): running quick query on the session store. Command I ran: ```redis-cli -h sessions-primary --scan | grep "session:token:" | xargs -L1 redis-cli -h sessions-primary ttl``` will take a sec. I have an export of tokens issued 02:00-02:15 UTC, saving to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1758888888/tokens.csv (access restricted).
jen (security): good. Start targeted revokes for tokens with src IP 35.198.22.14 first. Use rolling revokes to avoid mass customer impact. Plan: revoke tokens that show suspicious activity, then expand window if signals persist.
elaine (support): heads up — I already have one customer (acct: acme-0) pinging CS about 401s. Can we prepare a short template for CS staff?
jen (security): template ready, please use: "We're investigating intermittent 401s affecting session refresh. We're taking steps to secure tokens and will update within 1 hour. No action required from your side." Save in #support-templates.
tom (prod): quick check: are any CI/CD deploy keys in logs? I see a few truncated S3 paths referencing builds/ci/artifacts. I'll search CI logs.
kai (infra): found 3 debug uploads with metadata that looks like `build_id` and an env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in one archived debug bundle. That bundle lifespan was 02:10-02:11 and was uploaded to an internal S3 bucket. Access policy: private but lifecycle retention short. Taking a snapshot and rotating the bucket credentials.
jen (security): mark that bucket as suspected. Rotate its access keys (KMS integration). Steps: 1) create new keys, 2) update service accounts using new key, 3) invalidate old keys. I'll coordinate with infra.
marco (oncall): action items so far: WAF block (done), targeted token revokes (in progress), bucket key rotation (kai+j), support template posted. Anyone seeing customer-facing outages?
elaine (support): one customer reported degraded session refresh, others report transient 401s. No broad outage reported yet.
jen (security): escalate: create incident severity 2 — data exposure possible (tokens/leaked debug bundle). Notifying legal and privacy. @ops-bot please create the incident doc and add pager notes.
ops-bot: Incident doc created: https://internal.redwood/incident/1758888888 — added runbook checklist: token_revoke -> key_rotate -> notify_customers -> postmortem.
marco (oncall): executing token revoke script now (rolling): ```python tools/revoke_tokens.py --source-ip 35.198.22.14 --dry-run false``` — script started, estimated 6 minutes.
kai (infra): rotated S3 bucket keys, updated IAM role to use new key, old keys disabled. Confirmed no access after rotate.
jen (security): good. After revoke run completes, we'll run a sweep for suspicious refresh attempts from other IPs. If tokens stored in logs are present, rotate service tokens referenced in those logs as well.
tom (prod): I'm throttling refresh endpoint to add a short-term rate limit for anonymous token issuers: ```nginx limit_req zone=authburst burst=50 nodelay;``` — deploying a small config change now.
marco (oncall): revoke run finished. 142 tokens invalidated in targeted window. No evident errors in downstream services; minor CS tickets only.
jen (security): plan next 2 hours: 1) full token sweep for 24h window, 2) rotate any service keys found in logs, 3) legal/privacy notification updated with scope, 4) prepare customer outbound for impacted tenants.
elaine (support): prepping outbound — will coordinate with legal and account teams for targeted notify. ETA 45m for first customer emails.
marco (oncall): handing to @jen for post-rotation monitoring and to close once legal confirms notification. I'll remain available for questions. If anything else flares, ping the channel. :lock: :thumbsup:
jen (security): taking post-rotation lead. I'll post a summary in 30m with indicators of compromise and the final token count. Thanks team."
